evidence.experimental_conditions: Dermal sensitization followed by ear challenge; Protocol 1 and Protocol 2 (exact doses and timepoints not specified in this text window).
evidence.support_text: Upon ear challenge, TMA-sensitized mice had significant ear swelling compared to their vehicle control groups as measured by the MEST. The additional dermal sensitization (Protocol 2) demonstrated an increased contact hypersensitivity response, with statistically significant increases at both 24 and 48 h post-challenge compared to Protocol 1.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Mice challenged on ear; ear swelling measured 48 hours after challenge
evidence.support_text: The MEST did not identify CIN as a contact allergen because ear swelling was not observed 48 hours after ear challenge.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 5% benzalkonium chloride (BAC) topically applied to mouse ears; C57BL/6 mice; ear swelling measured after 24 hrs.
evidence.support_text: Maximal increases of ear thickness were determined in TNCB- compared to BAC-treated ears after 24 hrs, indicating BAC did not induce significant hapten-specific ear swelling.

evidence.experimental_conditions: at SD50 dose (0.040 mg/kg)
evidence.support_text: At the SD50, the mean ear swelling for the group was 0.020 mm and for mice demonstrating positive responses it was 0.037 mm.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 0.01% MDI for sensitization; challenge dose not specified; mice; ear swelling measured but background irritation noted
evidence.support_text: We chose 0.01% MDI for sensitization. Upon challenge, MDI produced a relatively high background in ear swelling, presumably due to irritation. However, the ear swelling was much higher in the sensitized mice.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 0.04% DNFB in acetone for sensitization; challenge dose not specified; mice; ear swelling measured 48 h post-challenge
evidence.support_text: Upon sensitization with 0.04% DNFB in acetone, a significant increase in ear swelling was observed that peaked at 48 h after challenge, while ear swelling was not observed in unsensitized mice.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 2.5% TMA for sensitization; 25% TMA for challenge; mice; ear swelling measured but peak not specified
evidence.support_text: We chose 2.5% TMA for sensitization and 25% TMA for elicitation. Under these conditions, moderate but significant ear swelling was observed, while no swelling was observed in unsensitized mice.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 25 µL of 0.13% MI in OOA vehicle applied to dorsal side of both ears for three consecutive days (days 0-2); Mus musculus.
evidence.support_text: Application of MI at a concentration of 0.13% for three consecutive days induced statistically significant ear swelling (p<0.001) as shown in Fig. 2a.

evidence.experimental_conditions: 25 µL of 0.4% MI in OOA vehicle applied to dorsal side of both ears for three consecutive days (days 0-2); Mus musculus.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Challenge performed in sensitized mice with varying doses (referenced from Scott et al., 2002)
evidence.support_text: Squaric acid dibutyl ester was tested in sensitized mice by measuring mean ear thickness after challenge. The ear thickness increased dose-dependently, indicating a positive skin sensitization result (Scott et al., 2002).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Challenge with GST; mouse; positive threshold 20% increase in ear thickness; induction by topical treatment with GST prior.
evidence.support_text: In the mouse ear swelling test, positive ear swelling (20% greater increase in ear thickness) after challenge with GST was shown in 2 out of 6 mice those previously treated with GST.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Colophony pretreatment on mouse flank skin using acetone/oil vehicle, followed by challenge with colophony; compared to acetone/oil vehicle alone.
evidence.support_text: Colophony pretreatment of mouse skin led to a slight overall increase in ear thickness on challenge, but this did not differ significantly from that seen in mice treated with the acetone/oil vehicle alone (24 hours, p = 0.21; 48 hours, p = 0.91).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Female C57BL/6J mice; sensitized by injection of NiSO4 into the oral mucosa; challenged; ear swelling measured at 48 hr
evidence.support_text: Oral mucosa sensitization with NiSO4 succeeded in all mice. Ear swelling was significantly greater in the skin- than in the oral mucosa-sensitized mice at 48 hr after challenge.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Female C57BL/6J mice; sensitized by injection of NiSO4 into the oral mucosa; single oral administration of NiSO4 (oral tolerance) before challenge; ear swelling measured at 48 hr
evidence.support_text: Ear swelling was suppressed by single oral administration of NiSO4 in both the skin- and oral mucosa-sensitized mice to the level of that in non-sensitized mice.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Female C57BL/6J mice; sensitized by injection of NiSO4 into the skin; challenged; ear swelling measured at 48 hr

evidence.experimental_conditions: Female C57BL/6J mice; sensitized by injection of NiSO4 into the skin; single oral administration of NiSO4 (oral tolerance) before challenge; ear swelling measured at 48 hr
evidence.support_text: Ear swelling was suppressed by single oral administration of NiSO4 in both the skin- and oral mucosa-sensitized mice to the level of that in non-sensitized mice.

evidence.experimental_conditions: MI-sensitized mice (various concentrations) challenged with BIT (concentration not specified).
evidence.support_text: All MI-sensitized subgroups showed a statistically significant increase in ear swelling when challenged with BIT compared to control mice (p<0.001 overall). Pair-wise comparisons for BIT challenge showed partly significant differences between sensitization groups.

evidence.experimental_conditions: MI-sensitized mice (various concentrations) challenged with OIT (concentration not specified).
evidence.support_text: All MI-sensitized subgroups, regardless of sensitization concentration, showed a statistically significant increase in ear swelling when challenged with OIT compared to control mice (p<0.001 overall). Pair-wise comparisons for OIT challenge showed partly significant differences between sensitization groups.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Mice sensitized by epicutaneous application of MI at 0.13%, 0.4%, or 1.2% w/v on day 1, 2, 8, and 9, and challenged on day 23 with MI (concentration not specified, but exception involves 0.4% MI challenge). Ear swelling measured 24-48 h after challenge.
evidence.support_text: In MI-sensitized mice challenged with MI, all subgroups except those sensitized with 0.13% MI and challenged with 0.4% MI showed a statistically significant increase in ear swelling compared to control mice (p<0.001). Additional pair-wise comparisons demonstrated a significant concentration-dependent trend in ear swelling when mice were sensitized with 0.13%, 0.4%, or 1.2% MI and challenged with MI.
